purpose: Supplementary data-only checkpoint across US, British, German, Soviet and Japanese primary-source routes with Finnish cross-checks. Digitized trace points retain source speed labels and uncertainty. No values are activated in the solver.

sources.report: NACA MR L5B13b / WR L-717, stalling characteristics, 1945
sources.notes: Same campaign as the earlier coefficient and condition rows. Plots label speed indicated. Part I instrumentation supports a corrected speed definition in Part I, while the Part III trace processing and per-run fuel or weight remain unresolved.

sources.report: NACA MR L5B13 / WR L-715, longitudinal stability, 1945
sources.notes: Position-corrected static pressure and standard sea-level compressibility for Part I service indicated speed. Low-speed formation against trailing-head-calibrated aircraft. No numerical error curve or proof of Part III processing in these pages.

sources.report: NACA RM L8A06, longitudinal stability and stalling, 1948
sources.notes: The bottom panel of Figure 52 has one service indicated airspeed trace and a NACA emblem. The earlier paired-channel record is superseded by this inspection.

sources.report: NACA TN 2675, lateral/directional companion, reprint of RM L6L31
sources.notes: Identifies the calibrated NACA right-wing boom, low-speed formation method and pressure-based CAS definition. L8A06 cites the earlier lateral report for instrumentation. Keep the L8A06 traces under their published label pending an explicit processing link.

sources.report: T.O. 01-25CH-1 Flight Operating Instructions, 20 June 1943
sources.notes: Verified 63-page alternate PDF. Ratings, approximate IAS stall values and generic loading examples. The ratings are not specific to runs on 41-13635. 61 inHg requires the specified boost-control modification.

sources.report: Messerschmitt Bedienungsvorschrift-Fl, Reg. Nr. 249, June 1942
sources.location: Printed 12–15, PDF 19–22, and cooling procedure at printed 17
sources.notes: The rating table lists emergency power. Pages 13 and 15 explicitly bar its use and say it is blocked. Printed sea-level best-climb 250 km/h is struck out and annotated 270 on this copy. No authorization for the handwritten change or numbers for the higher altitude cells are established.

sources.aircraft: Ki-84, Japanese airframe documentation, no test serial stated
sources.report: PACMIRS Air Translations No. 8, captured Japanese Doc 1578, sections 1–6, 26 July 1945
sources.notes: Translated June–August 1944 Japanese instructions captured at Mabalacat on 27 January 1945. The translator explicitly notes overlap with ADVATIS Translation 92. No claim that handbook tables reproduce a documented flight by serial 302 or establish actual mass or calibrated stall speed.

sources.report: Focke-Wulf Flugbericht 210001 Nr. 1, 10 October 1944
sources.notes: Existing report B11. Eltron and Bruhn comparison at level-flight speeds confirms installation dependence. The scan does not establish WNr 210002 near-stall correction.

sources.aircraft: Fw 190 D-9 WNr 210002 with alternate Jumo 213 A
sources.report: Focke-Wulf Flugbericht 210002 Nr. 4, 1 March 1945
sources.notes: Polished surface, sealed engine gap, guns without ammunition. The replacement engine did not shift to the high blower. Table distinguishes WNr 210002 earlier and replacement engines and WNr 210001. Rows for earlier engines reproduce earlier flights.

sources.aircraft: Spitfire LF Mk IX BS543, Merlin 66

sources.notes: Original plot verifies serial, 7,485 lb take-off and open radiators. The textual report explicitly transfers BF274 PEC for matching heads. No original Table II scan or sub-100 mph calibration recovered. Same BS543 test as prior values.

sources.aircraft: Spitfire F Mk IX BF274, Merlin 61

sources.aircraft: Spitfire LF Mk IX MA648, Merlin 66

sources.location: Original Figure 1 linked on report page. Transcript §§2.1–4.2.
sources.notes: Existing independent-check source, retained as separate fuel pump and long-intake configuration. Main test weight 7,380 lb. Comparison table reports a separate 7,000 lb figure. Summary and comparison table differ by 100 ft on the FS critical altitude.

sources.report: RAE Aero 1906 / ARC 7424, drag and trim changes at high Mach
sources.location: ARC R&M 2222 bibliography entry 98 and R&M 2748 reference 1
sources.notes: High-Mach flight-test locator. R&M 2748 studies Meteor drag and is not a substitute for this report. Exact fighter specimens and usable domain await the original.

sources.report: ARC R&M 2609, comparison of stalling characteristics
sources.notes: Prototype flow breakaway and qualitative stall behavior only. No transfer to the LF IX benchmark.

sources.report: NACA MR L4L18 high-speed performance, 18 December 1944
sources.notes: Earlier report R01. Kollsman head at 0.35 wing chord ahead and reference static at 0.94 chord. High-speed report on a different aircraft, not the correction for 43-24777.

sources.report: NACA WR L-547 rudder and sideslip, October 1942
sources.notes: Earlier source lead reviewed at page level. Pilot meter and recorder shared a research boom one chord ahead of the left tip. The boom is distinct from the service installation. Yaw calibration is not an IAS correction.

sources.report: Focke-Wulf Flugbericht 665 Nr. 1, Eastern Front fairings
sources.location: PDF 1 conditions and PDF 2 combat-power speed plot
sources.notes: 3827 kg fully fueled and 2400 rpm. Two MG 17 and two MG 151, ammunition ballast, tight cowling. Fixed wheel fairings and lower gear fairings removed for the Eastern Front tests. Tailwheel extended or retracted. Keep distinct from WNr 783.

sources.report: Focke-Wulf Flugbericht 670 Nr. 1, January 1943
sources.notes: ETC 501 and underwing Ju 87 racks. With tanks the aircraft developed strong aileron buffeting from 380 km/h indicated and the top speed could not be established. Separate report without tanks/bomb compared with WNr 669; neither is a clean WNr 783 result.

sources.location: Modern reproduction of the period digest text
sources.notes: Original run sheets and actual engine settings are unverified. Prior pack already identifies the airframe. A separate captured aircraft from the German 783 benchmark.

series.source_location: PDF 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, and condition table on PDF 4
series.conditions: Window bracketed visually from initial roll departure and change in normal-force trace. Published take-off weight approximately 11200 lb. Run weight, altitude and fuel are unavailable in these figure captions. Speed spread is an approximate reading/selection bound. Normal acceleration band is approximate around the first break. Powered and flap-down traces represent their stated propwash and configuration.
series.notes: indicated mph, exact correction status unverified

series.source_location: PDF 70, 72, 75, 77, 78 and configuration table on PDF 3
series.conditions: Near-break or minimum approach window. The approach trace has no clear full-break marker. All rows are observed trace readings with visual bounds, same flight-test program. Power off is the report condition, not an assumed zero shaft torque.
rows: early minimum-speed window with all controls
series.notes: service indicated mph, explicitly labeled, CAS mapping pending

series.conditions: Normal operational loads. The table does not give test weight, serial or a correction curve. The landing section says the approximate 82 mph figure can vary by 2 mph with load.

100 octane chart. Critical altitudes are labeled with ram where given. Military chart rounds the printed text 48.24 to 48.2 inHg. WEP hardware must be modified to reach 61 inHg and WEP selection uses low blower below 8000 ft and high above. No WEP duration number in chart.
Generic worked configurations from the handbook, not a weigh sheet for 41-13635. Full internal example is distinct from the 8505 lb design load.

Emergency entries in the rating table were blocked under the instructions on pp.13 and 15. No time limit is supplied by this table. Apply the 18 June order and engine-specific restrictions where relevant. The Finnish April 1943 test remains 2540 actual rpm, 2580 indicated, per the existing secondary transcription.

Fully equipped at 2000 m. Exact weight, serial and power unavailable. Final column is suspiciously labeled as elevator-tab turns despite values 1000–1200 and translator sic marks, so it is retained without reinterpretation. The source km/h is preserved. The mph column is a unit conversion rounded to one decimal with no airspeed correction.
Handbook table, test method and exact specimen unestablished. Boost figures retained in source units, with blanks left blank. Blower/status text is recorded only where printed.

Instructions call for military power with boost override unused and cowl flaps ordinarily fully open, cylinder temperature at or below 230 C. The gear-change instruction says temporarily reduce to 2600 rpm. Table prints 2900 rpm throughout and an unresolved +80 at 9000 m. Climb ceiling blank in translation. Flight origin, run mass and airframe not established.
Operational recommendations in the translated provisional handbook. The 3200 rpm restriction is a short-time low-boost limit, not a power rating.
rows: short overspeed, boost must be below value shown

series.conditions: Values as reported. 210002 checked A engine had a sealed gap/polished finish and no ammunition in Nr.4. The first and third columns summarize earlier flights. Conditions and serials must stay separate.

series.source_location: PDF 1 conditions and PDF 2 combat-power speed plot
series.conditions: Flight tests in Eastern Front fairing configurations. Fully fueled weight. Reported armament had ammunition ballast. Values qualify the existing high-speed curve for WNr 665.

series.speed_basis: indicated speed for buffet, source-level speed difference for comparison
series.conditions: Jabo configuration. Tanks installed caused buffet. The level speed difference compares separate aircraft and rack fairings without tanks or bomb.
rows: WNr 670 smaller rack fairing versus WNr 669 prototype fairing

calibration_reviews.decision: Part I corrected service-indicated definition is explicit there. Part III plot label and no run-weight or raw reduction record preclude labeling the digitized traces certified CAS. The apparent spread between same-condition Figures 6 and 7 (roughly 76 vs 66 mph at the first departure on visual inspection) also deserves investigation before an automatic mapping.

One service-indicated trace per checked chart. The winged NACA emblem is a watermark. TN 2675 confirms corrected instrumentation method, but a numerical correction or explicit link to L8A06 processing is still absent. Do not apply handbook PEC to the NACA trace.
No serial, exact test weight, pitot calibration or matched power established. The general weight-and-balance chart does not supply the weight at which the stall table was measured.
No explicit speed basis, mass, boost, or serial in stall table. Keep separate from 302 flight tests and TAIC estimates.
